messages.author: 2710b717e5dbb066
messages.subject: Re: Shading regions with different "designs"
parts:
You might want to start by asking why you want to do this.  While there may be legitimate reasons (others have pointed out that some people like to read books/articles on electronic devices that don't do color) many of the cases where people want to do this, it really is not the correct thing to do.  Even simple patterns like slanted lines can lead to a Moire effect which can distort the visual impact of the graph and/or make it more difficult to read, more complicated patterns can quickly become chart junk and you can find that the "art" is overpowering the "data".  If you find yourself going in that direction so that the graph is more eye-catching, then it may be time to replace the graph with a picture of a kitten.

Patterns have not been a priority for the developers of ggplot2, so I don't think there is a way to do it within ggplot2 (a feature rather than a bug to some of us).  But if you feel that you have a good reason and really want something like this, then there are additional tools such as Imagemagick, Gimp, and Inkscape (these are the free ones that I am familiar with, there are commercial ones as well and possibly other free ones) that ca be used to replace a block of color with a pattern or something else.  That route may be easier in the long run than trying to force ggplot2 to do it for you.

One other option that you may be able to adapt is there are some answers on stackoverflow where people wanted to use custom images as points in scatterplots. Those answers may point you in a useful direction.
